Stage 1: Input Processing & Embedding

• Input Formulation: [CLS] + tokens + [SEP] for structured tasks

Query, Key, Value = Linear(Input)

• Propagation Mechanism: Residual connections + layer normalization

2.2 Feed-Forward Network
FFN(x) = max(0, xW₁ + b₁)W₂ + b₂

• Purpose: Position-wise non-linear transformation
• Interaction: Independent processing per token position

2.3 Residual Connections & Normalization
LayerOutput = LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x))

• Gradient Flow: Mitigates vanishing gradient problem
• Training Stability: Enables deep network optimization

Vertical Flow (Through Layers):
• Layer 1: Local syntax, shallow patterns
• Middle Layers: Semantic relationships, dependencies
• Upper Layers: High-level reasoning, task-specific features

Horizontal Flow (Within Layers):

• Decoding Strategy: Greedy, beam search, or sampling

1. Information Mixing: Each layer increases receptive field, global context accumulates progressively

3. Computational Parallelism: Within-layer: All tokens processed simultaneously, attention quadratic in sequence length

Multi-Head Attention Configuration in Transformer Architectures

Core Configuration Pattern

MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head₁, head₂, ..., headₕ)Wᵒ

Where each head is computed as: headᵢ = Attention(QWᵢᵠ, KWᵢᴷ, VWᵢⱽ)

Typical Head Configurations by Model Scale

1. Base Models (∼100M parameters)
• Heads (h): 8-12 attention heads
• Model Dimension (d_model): 512-768
• Head Dimension (d_k = d_v): d_model / h ≈ 64 dimensions per head

2. Large Models (∼500M-1B parameters)
• Heads (h): 16-24 attention heads
• Model Dimension (d_model): 1024-1536
• Head Dimension (d_k = d_v): 64 dimensions per head

3. Very Large Models (∼10B+ parameters)
• Heads (h): 32-96 attention heads
• Model Dimension (d_model): 4096-8192
• Head Dimension (d_k = d_v): 128 dimensions per head

Dimension Splitting Mathematics

Standard Implementation:
d_model = h × d_k
d_k = d_v = d_model / h

Projection Dimensions:
• Q, K, V projections: Each is dimension [d_model × d_k]
• Output projection: Dimension [h × d_v × d_model]
• Total parameters per attention layer: 4 × d_model × d_model

Head Specialization Patterns

Different heads typically learn specialized functions:
• Local Attention Heads: Focus on adjacent tokens
• Syntax Heads: Capture grammatical relationships
• Long-Range Heads: Connect distant but related concepts
• Positional Heads: Track relative positions
• Content-Based Heads: Focus on semantic similarity

Configuration Trade-offs

More Heads:
• ✅ Better parallelization of different attention patterns
• ❌ Higher computational overhead for projections

Larger Head Dimensions:
• ✅ Richer representation per attention pattern
• ❌ Increased memory requirements

Modern Architectural Trends

• Grouped Query Attention (GQA): Shared K/V projections across head groups
• Multi-Query Attention (MQA): Single K/V projection across all heads
• Sliding Window Attention: Limited context to reduce computation
